- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or shows strong downward momentum, model often underestimates; increase forecast to reflect risk of rebound.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots and fails to correct — apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 5–10% for the next 3–5 periods.
- When sentiment is neutral or volatile (±0.2–0.5), model often fails to capture mean reversion — adjust forecast to align with recent 7–14 day moving average.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after a high, model often continues upward — apply “lag correction”: delay forecast peak by 2–4 periods if sentiment is weak.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to be overly optimistic when sentiment is positive — apply a “sentiment decay” rule: reduce forecast by 1–3% per day if sentiment >0.7 for 5+ consecutive days.
- If sentiment turns negative after a peak, model often fails to recognize the reversal — adjust forecast downward by 5–10% for next 3–5 periods.
